title: Every tasbih is charity
hook: the poor ask how to match the rich, and are told every glorification, praise and good word is charity (Nawawi 25, Abu Dharr)
tomorrow: your body owes something every morning. what, and to whom?

segments.voice: Yesterday God forbade oppression for Himself and among all His servants: no oppression, not in the palace and not at the tip jar. Today, people with nothing to give find out what they're holding.

Click, click, click: prayer beads moving through a grandmother's fingers, one bead per phrase. Meanwhile the fundraiser table, the donation link, the round-up at checkout can make giving feel like a club for people with money. In al-Nawawi's twenty-fifth hadith, some poor companions come to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, with a complaint that sounds very current. The wealthy have taken all the reward. They pray as we pray, fast as we fast, and give charity from their extra money. So the poor say the rich get it all. What's the answer? It's in that sound.
screen: `CLICK, CLICK, CLICK.` → `THE RICH GET ALL THE REWARD.` → `THE ANSWER IS A SOUND.`

segments.voice: From Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase: hasn't Allah given you things to give? Every tasbih, saying subhanallah, glory be to Allah, is charity. Every takbir, Allahu akbar, is charity. Every alhamdulillah is charity. Every la ilaha illallah is charity. Telling someone to do good is charity; stopping a wrong is charity. Look at what just happened. A word, the cheapest thing a person owns, gets moved into the column of giving. The poor companions weren't told the rich were wrong to give. They were handed a treasury they'd been carrying all along. Nobody has to wait for a paycheck to start giving. And this hadith runs on the ears. A tasbih is a sound: a phrase said softly, often counted on beads or on the fingers, so the counting itself has a texture, bead after bead, joint after joint. The hadith treats that sound as currency. Something to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, a whispered glory be to Allah sits in the same column as a gift of money. And the money isn't canceled either: give what you have, and add the words. Every glory is a gift.
screen: `HASN'T ALLAH GIVEN YOU THINGS TO GIVE?` · `EVERY TASBIH IS CHARITY.` · `A TREASURY THEY ALREADY HAD.` · `A SOUND, COUNTED AS A GIFT.` · then, large: `EVERY GLORY IS A GIFT.`

segments.voice: Say a short phrase of praise or thanks softly, again and again, at the pace of your breath, counting on the joints of your fingers. If you pray, subhanallah fits; if not, a plain thank you works. Let a bead, or the press of a thumb on a knuckle, keep the time, and listen to the sound more than the count.
Every tasbih is charity: each word of glory, counted as a gift. The hadith's answer to people with no money to give.
Keep this one: every glory is a gift, even the quietest one, said under your breath. Hadith twenty-five, said softly.

screen: `DAY 1453 COUNTS.` → `THE FORTY · 25 OF 42.` → `TOMORROW: YOUR BODY OWES SOMETHING EVERY MORNING. WHAT, AND TO WHOM?`

howItsDone: Many Muslims say subhanallah, alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar after prayers, counting on prayer beads (a misbaha or tasbih) or on their fingers.

original.note: Arabic: charity, a gift freely given; in this hadith, stretched to cover words.

trapdoor: what you thought: charity means money.
what it means: each glorification, praise and good word counts as charity: a treasury for people with no money.
what a scholar hears: Sahih Muslim 1006 (Abu Dharr); the list goes on past words to deeds, including within marriage, which the commentaries discuss.

chat.says: masjid fundraiser night. i have $4 lol. dadi just handed me her tasbih. is that a hint?
options: kind of. give the $4, and the words too; each tasbih counts as charity.
it means skip giving money; dhikr replaces it, so keep the $4.
it means $4 is too small to give, so just pray for the cause.
chat.meaning: The hadith opens a treasury of words to people without money; it doesn't cancel giving what you can.

tasbih.meaning: saying subhanallah, glory be to Allah; also the beads

takbir.meaning: saying Allahu akbar, God is greater

la ilaha illallah.meaning: there is no god but God

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major hadith collection, compiled by Imam Muslim
